Subject: VAT classification + PO remit for Redwood purchases

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. One operational question came up while preparing our master vendor form: we sell into both the UK and Ireland but operate from a single UK legal entity. For Redwood's PO/AR process — do you need a separate remit/PO entity for IE purchases to handle VAT reverse charge, or can we route all POs to the UK entity and provide VAT invoices that note reverse charge treatment?

Also attaching our VAT certificate and bank remittance stub. If there's a specific field or code you require on the PO for non-UK VAT treatment (reverse charge / zero-rate), let me know and we can include it in our bookkeeping to speed up invoice matching.

Best,
Simon Clark
Head of Finance, Acme Supplies Ltd.
Attachments: ACME_VAT_CERTIFICATE_2027.pdf (application/pdf), ACME_bank_details_qr.pdf (image/png)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: VAT classification + PO remit for Redwood purchases

Thanks Simon — good question and useful attachments. Quick answers up front: 1) You can route POs to the UK legal entity; we do not require a separate PO entity for IE if your invoices clearly show the applicable VAT treatment and tax identifiers. 2) We DO need the VAT number shown on the invoice and a clear line item/annotation if the reverse charge applies.

A few operational asks so our AP team can set this up without delays:
- Please confirm the legal entity name that should appear on Redwood's PO (exact text).
- Confirm the VAT registration number for both UK and any Irish registration if present.
- Provide a signed Supplier Tax Residency Form (attached template) so our tax team has the paperwork for cross-border withholding/recordkeeping.
- If you expect invoices to include reverse-charge lines, add the annotation: "Reverse charge – Article 196 (or local equivalent) applied. Customer liable for VAT." in the invoice notes.

Ben — can you advise whether we need to split PO "bill to" vs "remit to" in Coupa (or our PO system) for Acme, or can we use a single PO entity and set remittance details on the invoice match?

Simon, I'll loop in AP contact Laura for the next steps. If you can return the signed residency form and confirm the entity name by end of week, we can provision POs within 5 business days.

Cheers,
Evelyn Hart
Procurement Manager, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 12:48:00 -0400
Subject: Re: VAT classification + PO remit for Redwood purchases

Eve/Laura — short answer: single PO entity is fine for Acme provided we capture two fields at invoice time: 1) VAT ID (for supplier) and 2) Invoice VAT treatment code (e.g., RC = reverse charge, STD = standard VAT, EX = exempt). Our matching engine will enforce that if RC is present we do not apply UK VAT on Redwood's side and we post for reverse charge when reconciling.

Operational notes:
- Coupa (prod) can store a separate remit bank account on the vendor profile; we set that to the UK account supplied. No need for two vendor IDs unless Acme requests separate legal entity POs.
- We do need the signed residency form and evidence (VAT cert) to satisfy AP audit.
- If Acme expects netting across country subsidiaries, request a vendor-entity-split ticket and legal review. That's likely unnecessary here.

I'll add a small internal checklist for Laura to get this completed.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Tax & Compliance, Redwood Inference
